channel.description: Latest articles from West Hawaii Today (westhawaiitoday.com)

item.title: Barrage of GOP state bills seeks vast trans restrictions
item.description: After a year in which the Trump administration has pressed to limit the ways Americans can identify as transgender in public life, Republicans are pushing the issue at the state level with new zeal.

item.title: New Mexico probes allegation of bodies buried near Epstein ranch
item.description: New Mexico’s Department of Justice said on Wednesday the state was investigating an allegation, which emerged from documents released by the U.S. Department of Justice, that the late sex offender Jeffrey Epstein ordered the bodies of two foreign girls buried outside his remote New Mexico ranch.

item.title: At Board of Peace debut, Trump announces global commitments for Gaza reconstruction
item.description: U.S. President Donald Trump told the first meeting of his Board of Peace on Thursday that nations had contributed $7 billion to a Gaza reconstruction fund that aims to rebuild the enclave once Hamas disarms, an objective that is far from becoming a reality. item.title: ‘Spamalot’ kicks of tonight at Aloha Theatre
item.description: The Aloha Performing Arts Company proudly presents “Monty Python’s Spamalot,” the outrageously funny, Tony Award-winning musical that skewers the legend of King Arthur and the Knights of the Round Table.

item.title: State bill would fund a sanctuary pilot program for homeless women, children
item.description: Homeless women and children under age 18 would be able to live in their vehicles or in a communal tent on government-sanctioned land that would offer security, case management and bathroom and laundry services under a Senate bill under consideration at the state Legislature.

item.title: It’s been a wet month so far in East Hawaii, but drought persists
item.description: February is the shortest month of the year, but this month has been long on rainfall in East Hawaii.

item.title: King Charles’ brother Andrew released after arrest over misconduct relating to Epstein
item.description: AYLSHAM, England — King Charles’ younger brother Andrew Mountbatten-Windsor was released from police custody on Thursday evening after being arrested on suspicion of misconduct in public office over allegations he sent confidential government documents to Jeffrey Epstein.

item.title: Trump warns Iran of ‘bad things’ if no deal made, appears to set deadline of 10-15 days
item.description: WASHINGTON — President Donald Trump warned Iran on Thursday that it must make a deal over its nuclear program or “really bad things” will happen, and appeared to set a deadline of no more than 10 to 15 days before the U.S. might take action.

item.title: Dems choose Spanberger to deliver State of the Union response to Trump
item.description: WASHINGTON — Democrats have selected Gov. Abigail Spanberger of Virginia to deliver their party’s response to President Donald Trump’s State of the Union address Tuesday, putting at center stage a former congresswoman who flipped a red seat to blue ahead of midterm elections in which they are expecting to win back control of the House.

item.title: US trade deficit swells in December as imports surge; labor market holding steady
item.description: WASHINGTON — The U.S. trade deficit widened sharply in December amid a surge in imports, and the goods shortfall in 2025 was the highest on record despite President Donald Trump’s tariffs on foreign manufactured merchandise.
